goal: Add a reference implementation of OP_CAT (BIP-347) so developers and researchers can build and test against it
Lets downstream forks like bitcoin-inquisition experiment with CAT without waiting on Bitcoin Core consensus code
Does not include any activation or signaling logic itself
reviewability: Paused: a maintainer moved this to draft pending concept consensus for OP_CAT in Tapscript
Reviewing the code now risks being moot if the concept direction changes before consensus forms
agreement: Concept-level dispute: no consensus yet that OP_CAT should be activated at all (achow101)
Nonblocking objection: proposed 'neutered CAT' compromise doesn't prevent the introspection tricks it targets (bigspider)
Technical questions on flag interactions were answered and implemented as new test cases (rot13maxi, Co1nB3e)
Code-level review comments from engaged reviewers were addressed by the author (ajtowns, rot13maxi, awin28522)

categories.name: validation
why: P1 because it's a proposed soft fork touching consensus-adjacent interpreter code and new script verify flags
Impact hinges on reaching a decision on activation and ensuring correctness if ever activated, not on the code alone
A maintainer explicitly paused it pending exactly that consensus decision

categories.name: mempool
why: P3 because the new DISCOURAGE_OP_CAT policy flag is a no-op today with no relay or DoS impact
Its value is entirely contingent on a future activation decision that remains unresolved

categories.name: tests
why: P2 because it adds substantial new JSON, unit, and functional test coverage for OP_CAT
New #SCRIPT#/#CONTROLBLOCK# macros make writing Tapscript JSON tests much easier project-wide
This tooling could help future Tapscript test-writing regardless of whether OP_CAT is ever activated
